utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We will have the witness in now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation that's shown to you on the card now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, I believe, has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Mr. Milasinovic, good morning. Before we begin our work, I'm going to ask you, as we speak the same language, to wait for me to finish my question and then for you to make a small pause before you begin answering so that all the services could do their job properly and, thus, we will also do our job more quickly and more efficiently. Sir, could you please tell us something about yourself, your CV.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Radomir Milasinovic. I was born on the 17th of March, 1948, in Gornja Bukovica [Realtime transcript read in error "Lukovica"], municipality of Savnik, the Republic of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, it's Gornja Bukovica with a B, not with an L. Could you please tell us what your qualifications are.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: In 1971 I completed the faculty of political sciences at the university of Belgrade. I passed my masters at the same faculty in 1975. In 1978 I got my doctorate, doctor's degree, at the same faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm making this break just for your information in order for the transcript to pick up everything that we are saying, and I am kindly asking you to speak more slowly, please. Could you please tell us something about your professional career.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: My career began in 1972 when I got a job at the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. I worked there for three years, and then I moved to the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. I worked as the chief of the department for investigations, analysis, and information from 1983 until 1988. From 1988 I was working as a professor at the faculty of criminal sciences of the university in Zagreb. At the same time, I also lectured at the university of Ljubljana as a form of co-operation between universities where I taught international relations and security. And at the faculty of criminal sciences I taught the subject of security and international relations. From 1972 I've been working at the institute for criminological and sociological investigations until 2001, and then in 1982 I became the professor of international public law at the university in Pristina. From 2001 onwards, I am a tenured professor of the faculty of security of the university of Belgrade, and from 2004 I became the head of the department for security and the head of the institute for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milasinovic, page 3, line 5, it says from 1972 until 2001 that you worked there; is that correct? You mean from 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from 1992, when I was elected professor at the Pristina university for international public law, and I worked there until 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. This is just a correction because you had said 1972.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: I also worked at the police academy for three and a half years, and I taught criminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D011-5715.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And now we are looking at a short biography, your CV actually that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we give the witness a hard copy of the documents that we will be using for our examination-in-chief so that we can proceed more efficiently?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is document number 1 in your binder. This is your CV, and you know very well what it is. You don't have to look at it anymore. But I would like to ask you to tell us a little bit more about your professional and academic and educational activities as well as your studies of the organisation and the functioning of the security system.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: In the federal and the republican MUPs of Serbia and Yugoslavia, I was the chief of the department for investigation, analysis, information; I also worked on scientific research, analysis, and data processing, and we dealt with a lot of matters that had to do with organisation functioning and the overall work of the organ of the internal affairs both from the public security and the state security area. The federal minister appointed me as the chief inspector for republican and provincial organs of internal affairs, where we reviewed the organisation, the work, the overall functioning of all professional lines and activities of the organs of internal affairs. I also lectured foreign delegations, delegations from China and some other countries, from Asia and Africa, on the topic of the organisation and the functioning and the work of the organs of internal affairs. And as far as my scientific research is concerned, at the institute for criminology and sociology, I was also involved in projects focusing on the problems in the work of the organs of internal affairs and in their activities to uncover and suppress all activities threatening the activities of the state, and particularly the place and the role of the MUP organs in combatting the criminal activities inside and outside of the country. I published a number of works in scientific research magazines on my work. I participated in all congresses and consultations, domestically and internationally, which dealt with the work of the organs of internal affairs. I also edited some publications issued by the organs of the Republic of Serbia, accrediting all the scientific research and educational programmes at the police academy, the faculty for security, and the academy for security and diplomacy. I also did peer reviews of textbooks from these institutions and also reviewed some scientific research papers. And as chief of the department for security, I am very involved and up-to-date on all topics that have to do with security management, conflict resolution, theory of conflicts, the aetiology and occurrences of endangering security and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D00931, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D009-0959, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, the document is in tab 2 in your binder. We're now looking at your expert report, sir. We can all see that, and its titled: "The position and role of the chief of the public security department in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia in anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999." Would you be able to tell us a little bit more about your expert report.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence of General Vlastimir Djordjevic asked me to write an expert report on the position and the role of the chief of the public security department in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia in anti-terrorist activities in the period of 1998 and 1999, especially looking at anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo, especially focusing on that. Also, I was given the task in the broader context of explaining this function.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to tell us, how did you deal with these issues?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of positive legal regulations and documents that I had at my disposal and using my empirical knowledge, I approached the drafting of this analysis with the idea of attempting to explain the most relevant issues relating to the organisation and the functioning of the organs of internal affairs, the place, and the role of the public security department, and the particular place and role of the chief of the public security department in the context of anti-terrorist activities in the Ministry of Internal Affairs as it related to Kosovo and Metohija in the period of 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to tell us about the structure of your report and the methodology that you used?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: As for the structure, first of all, I explained the jurisdiction and the way the ministry is organised, their tasks, the management by the ministry, then the status of the members of the MUP personnel with special headings that deal with each of these issues. And in the end, I gave my opinion or my findings dictated by the data that I had at my disposal. As for the methodology, I used the general methodology and also some specialised methodology which is usually used in scientific research work. I used not only the methods used in social sciences, but also in exact sciences. And I focused mostly on the method of analysis of the context and also comparative analysis of the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us, would you change anything in your report?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't change anything in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, this appears to be a document which in the end reaches opinions or findings of the witness about matters which are directly in issue between the parties in this case and which are the subject of detailed evidence and upon which the Chamber in the end will have to reach its findings. As a matter of general expression, the witness appears to have studied the same documents or by and large the same documents that have been placed in evidence before the Chamber; and based upon those and based upon what he says is his empirical knowledge, he then reaches conclusions on some of the most central and critical facts. Now, is there not a problem with this document insofar as it does that? Because what it is doing is directly encroaching on the task of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I do agree with what you've said; however, the expert's task was not to adjudicate, rather to provide his opinion based on the documentation presented to him. He did not go into the examination of the numerous evidence we have; that is the task of the Chamber. Based on what I understood, the expert provided his opinion on the basis of the documents he reviewed and the legislation and decrees. He analysed the jurisdiction, organisation, and tasks of the MUP, placing within it the role of the chief of the security department and analysed the role based also on the activities performed by the chief in 1998 and 1999 in Kosovo. There can be no expert report without an opinion of the expert being expressed within it. Of course, the fact that the expert report is admitted into evidence does not necessarily mean that the opinion based -- expressed therein will be accepted as evidence. This is something that will be in the hands of the Trial Chamber. The expert report will either assist the Trial Chamber in their examination of the evidence or will not; in other words, the Chamber will either accept the conclusions presented by the expert or not. The idea was that within the legislative and regulatory framework in the documents we have in the case file, the witness should provide his opinion without going into what is the role of the Trial Chamber. He didn't go into witness statements or anything like that, and I do agree with what the -- Your Honour has said, that this is in fact more of a presentation in the light of the regulatory aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There are two issues perhaps, and your submissions may have rolled them together as one, that is, whether the Chamber will be assisted by somebody from his very impressive formal education and his experience in understanding and assessing the regulatory framework which governed the operation of the ministry. As distinct from that, there is the question of whether the witness, in following that task, has gone what we might say a step too far for legal purposes and has come to findings which are findings which are for this Chamber to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I may have made the mistake of proceeding from the idea of an expert report as it is envisaged under the Yugoslav jurisdiction. An expert report is on the same plain with all the other types of evidence, and it is up to the Trial Chamber to decide whether to attach any value to it or not. Now, pursuant to your decision rendered in relation to a submission from the OTP, my understanding was that you did point to some of the problematic issues existing in Mr. Milasinovic's report that the Trial Chamber would be mindful of in rendering its adjudication. Because in para 4 of that same decision, the Trial Chamber ruled that the expert should appear as a witness and that he would be testifying based on his report. If you believe that the expert's report encroaches upon the work of the Trial Chamber, I am prepared to withdraw the expert witness, since we do have a great deal of other evidence already in the case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that may be very tempting, it's not something we would want. On the contrary, we think we may well be very much assisted by what somebody with the knowledge and experience of the witness has to say. What I am saying is that this report not only canvasses the material and helps to open it up to understanding, but goes on to reach final conclusions or his words were "opinions or findings." And I just mention that to indicate that it's in that area where as a matter of legal procedure things may have gone too far. Now, I don't want to waste time today. We would prefer to hear the witness, but it may be that we should reflect upon this issue, and it may be that parts of the report have the difficulty that I mentioned that other parts do not, so that it could be that we could receive most or some of the report. You will understand that the essence of our decision was that there were a number of issues concerning the proposed evidence of the witness, which meant that it was much more practical and proper for the witness to give evidence orally so that some of these issues could be ventilated and debated as the thing progressed. What I'd suggest is that you proceed with your examination of the witness. We would consider in due course whether the report in its present form should be received or not, and in that regard we would value also receiving any submissions that Mr. Stamp may wish to make, he may prefer to make that during some later stage of the evidence of the evidence rather than right now. I leave that to his consideration because we don't want to interrupt your flow and waste time with the witness here on this legal question that we're posing to you. So can you proceed on that basis and understand that it may be that there are one or two answers that are given orally by the witness which we will come to see in the same category as this -- these pages that are recalled the findings or opinions of the witness, and we may deal with those specifically. Is that guidance enough to assist you and to enable us to get on with the evidence of the witness, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I reiterate that the mistake is mine because the structure of the report is one that is used in my jurisdiction in Serbia. The report does indeed have opinions and findings at the end, but they need not necessarily be admitted with the rest of the report. We have an analysis which is an objective presentation, and this should suffice for the Trial Chamber to draw its legal findings. My questions will not be related to the findings or will not elicit findings from the witness, but rather his knowledge on the workings of the MUP in this period of time. And I will not be asking for his legal opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We overlapped. What I said was: And that's where we will be assisted. So please carry on, Mr. Djurdjic, unless Mr. Stamp wants to put something at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I won't interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. Please, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Professor, can you tell us what kind of work is done by the internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The work related to the security of the Republic of Serbia which fall under the state security sector as well as work on uncovering all manner of activities which aim to undermine and disrupt the constitutional order of the country, criminal offences, border activities, protection of life and property of citizens and their security. All of these tasks fall within the remit of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us the basic classification of the affairs performed by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The main basic division of work is to the public security sector and the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the relevant period, that's to say 1998 and 1999, who had the competence of dealing with the internal affairs in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: It was the Ministry of the Interior which had that competence in that period of time in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what exactly is the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The MUP of Serbia is a government agency performing tasks conferred upon it by the parliament, the government, and the president of the republic, and of course, it performs activities falling within its competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the relevant period, who was it who headed the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: It was the minister of the interior of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who selected the minister of the interior, who elected him?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The minister was elected -- or is elected by the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia. The minister is a member of the government, and it represents the ministry and submits reports on the ministry's work to the parliament and the government. The minister is also charged with implementing laws and seeing to it that all the bylaws relate governing the work and role of the MUP staff issued, and of course his term of office is concurrent with that of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that the minister is an elected official in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: He is the only elected official of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What are the MUP minister's rights and obligations?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: His rights and obligations include the following: He represents the Ministry of the Interior, issues bylaws of general and specialised nature governing the work of the MUP, organises the work of the MUP, issues rules governing the work of the various organisational units within the MUP, is responsible for the work of the MUP staff, and as the only elected official of the MUP, he has the power to issue regulations governing the organisation of the MUP bodies and to implement regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is tab 3 in the batch of documents you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague, Madam O'Leary, instructs me that perhaps we should ask for the expert report to be MFI'd at this stage. But as I understood what you had to say, we would be doing that at the end of the expert's testimony. What am I to do? And of course I have to listen and hear out what my colleague, Madam O'Leary, has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document you have indicated or you have moved to be admitted into evidence, that motion is still alive. The Chamber has said rather than rule on it now, we will hear at some time Mr. Stamp and then reflect on that question, whether we will admit it, admit the whole of it or perhaps not some part of it or what, that's to be resolved. But it's there. We have it, and you have moved that it will be admitted into evidence. You're greatly assisted by Ms. O'Leary, as usual, but on this occasion, I would suggest that you can leave things as they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This piece of evidence is Law on Internal Affairs. Professor, I should like to ask you this: Bearing in mind Article 6 of this law, in what way was the MUP internally organised?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to rules governing the internal organisation of MUP, namely, rules governing the internal organisation of the public security sector and rules governing the internal organisation of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, these rules governing internal organisation of the MUP, who issued them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness because the speakers overlapped. Can he please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And who issued these rules?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There was one answer not heard, Mr. Djurdjic, because you moved on, and your voice overlapped with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that the minister issued the rules. You also started telling us what the competence of the Government of the Republic of Serbia was in this affair.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to give its consent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please pause before answering my question, otherwise not everything will be reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up P357.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is tab 5 in your binder. These are rules governing the internal organisation of the MUP. This is the consolidated text of the 31st of December, 1996.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Professor, do these rules apply to all the organisational units of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not to all the organisational units of the MUP. The rules apply to the protection of security and uncovering anti-constitutional activities. The rules also state that specialised rules would be issued governing the work of the state security sector; in other words, these rules apply only to the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up Article 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is page 3 in English and 2 in your version -- or rather, page 3. What you just said, is it laid out in Article 1?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Article 1 of the rules governing the internal organisation of the MUP dated the 5th of April, 1996, and it came into effect -- yes, those are the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up P1349, which is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 8 in your binder, but you will see it on your screen. There's no need for you to look at it there. These are rules governing the internal organisation of the state security sector?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: A moment ago we heard that the other rules governed only the internal organisation of the public security sector. Did there exist rules governing the organisation of both sectors in the same manner in this period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, there did not exist rules applying to both these sectors of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in what way were these two sectors linked in organisational terms?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, solely via the MUP minister because there did not exist an organisational body which would have been the intermediary between the minister and these two sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back to D357, rules governing the internal organisation of the MUP. This is tab 5. Which organisational units have been set out in these rules?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The public security sector units were laid out here, namely, the ones located in the head office of the public security sector of the MUP as well as the territorial units outside of the headquarters or the head office of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now call up -- or rather, turn to page 9 of the English version, Article 13 that is. Can you tell us which organisational units of the ministry were located in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The ten administrations and the operations centre were located in the headquarters, which had within their competence crime prevention, protection of life --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. We can read this.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: And the administrations consisted of departments, sectors, and groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, which territorial units were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: These were 33 secretariats of the internal affairs, and seven of those were located in the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija, seven of those in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, and the remainder in the rest of the territory of the Republic of Serbia. The secretariats had their internal affairs departments and police units in the various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did there exist subunits within the secretariats?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These organisational units were administrations which had their departments, sectors, and groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We also had organisational units outside of the sector?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: That was the MUP high school, MUP associate degree school, the MUP institute, and department for expert work and research.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These organisational units were set out in the rules governing the internal organisation of the MUP, as we can see. In addition to these organisational units, did the rules also envisage the possibility for other special units, organisational units and groups, to be set up?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The rules does indeed provide for the possibility of setting up special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we turn to page 6 in both versions, and I'm talking about the rules governing internal organisation. This is Article 6. Can you tell us who had the power of setting up these special, "Posebne," and "Specijalne" units in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: And the rules, it was the power vested with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This Article 6 of the rules on the internal organisation of the MUP also cover the state security department?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, because the state security department was organised pursuant to a different book of rules and its organisational units were covered by a different rule. This rule exclusively applied to the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see that in Article 10 of the rules, and this is on page 8 of the English version, there is the possibility of educating and -- of forming permanent and temporary staffs and working groups. Can you please tell us which departments this applies to and what are the specifics?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The minister of the interior, according to the rules, had the possibility of forming special staffs or organisational units, groups, commissions, and so on, which he could -- which could be set up by the chief of the public security department and the chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs from the public security department. These are the chiefs of the SUPs belonging to the public security department according to the territorial form of organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D100, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This should be a document in tab 9 in your binder, sir. We are seeing the decision on the forming of the staff of the ministry in Pristina dated the 15th of May, 1998, adopted by the assistant minister, the chief of the public security department, Vlastimir Djordjevic. Can you give us a brief analysis of this decision, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: This staff was formed pursuant to a decision by the department of the public security department pursuant to Article 10 of the rules of the internal organisation, and the staff is formed in order to plan, organise, direct, and co-ordinate the work of the secretariat of the interior in the police -- in the border police stations, or rather, in the SUPs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, and to carry out more complex and important duties that relate to suppressing civil unrest, terrorist acts, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And these duties are part of what?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: They are part of the duties of the public security department. All members of this staff are from the public security department, and they also comprise chief of the SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is heading the staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The staff is headed by the chief of the public security department, but he is always obliged to act pursuant to instructions of the minister. And if he does form a staff, he's duty-bound to immediately inform the minister of the interior about the establishment of such a staff. The staff was responsible to the chief of the public security department for its work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was at the head of the staff which was formed by the chief of the public security department?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The staff was headed by the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how was the reporting established pursuant to this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: This decision lays down that the Ministry of the Interior or the public security department would have to be informed about all matters pertaining to the area of work of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at now P760.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that is document in tab 10 in your binders. This is a decision on the composition of the staff and leaders for the staff that is supposed to cover the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. It was formed -- issued by the RJB chief, Vlastimir Djordjevic, on the 11th of June, 1998. Can you please briefly talk about the characteristics of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: This document states the personnel composition of the broader and the inner staff, and they are from the ranks of the public security department. The staff is being formed by the chief of the public security department --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You've already told us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit P57, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And this is in tab 11 in your binder, sir. This is a decision of the 16th of June, 1998, on the forming of the staff of the ministry for suppression of terrorism issued by the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic. Could you please tell us what the legal basis is for the issuance of this decision.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The legal basis for this decision is Article 7 of the Law on Internal Affairs, which allows for the possibility of organising the activities of the organs of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in view of the organisation provided for by the rules which refer to the public security and the state security departments, was there a possibility that this staff for the suppression of terrorism be formed in a different way?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: There was no legal possibility of forming it in a different way, and this is why the minister cited Article 7 of the Law on Internal Affairs because in the regulations governing the work of the public and state security department there is no article which would provide the opportunity to form an intra-department staff, in view of the fact that these are two different departments, and this would be an area -- or the staff that would be an inter-departmental one because the staff was dealing with this particular issue, and that is the suppression of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What are the characteristics of this decision issued by the minister?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: This decision is based on very characteristic legal grounds, and then the composition of the inner and the broader staff includes members of the public security department and the state security department, both in its narrower and broader composition. Its broader composition that included the chiefs of the secretariats of internal affairs and the chiefs of the centres of the state security department in -- centres in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: And of course the activities exclusively related to the KiM territory?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us how the decision defines the responsibility of the staff leader and the reporting back?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The responsibility is defined in such a way that the Chief of Staff was directly responsible to the Ministry [as interpreted] of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia and was not responsible to the public and state security department chiefs. And as far as informing and reporting back is concerned, the minister of internal affairs was supposed to be directly reported to, the minister of the internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Line 20 I would just like a correction, it says the ministry and it actually should state the minister.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how the tasks are defined in this decision.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The decision defines the tasks in such a way that the staff manages, organises, engages, directs, and executes, or rather, plans anti-terrorist actions in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija using the regular forces as well as attached and formed units that both deal with anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the decision it says that they are supposed to plan, organise, and control the work and the engagement of the organisational units of the ministry in the KiM. Can you please tell us which organisational units are those of the ministry in the KiM?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Those organisational units were the secretariats of internal affairs and the centres, seven SUPs, and centres -- there were three centres of the public security department, there were particular units --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. You said three centres of which department?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The state security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you please tell us -- tell us, which are the attached units or the sent units, what are those units?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: These are special units, Posebna Jedenice Policije, SAJ, Specijalne Antiteroristicke Jedinice, and the JSO, Jedinica za Specijalne Operacije.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And which department did the JSO belong to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The JSO belonged to the state security department and the SAJ belonged to the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that this staff was an inter-departmental one by its nature?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us then that whether the chief of the staff for the suppression of terrorism could have been responsible both to the minister and the chiefs of the departments?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the staff was responsible solely to the minister and not to the public and state security departments, this was not possible. Because the decision specified that the chief of the HQ would be responsible for his work exclusively to the minister of the internal affairs of the republic. And this arises from the fact that the chiefs of the public and the state security departments could not issue assignments and tasks to each other. And since there was no body between the ministry, the minister, and the public security department, this was laid down in this way in the decision in -- on the forming of the ministry staff for the suppression of terrorism for the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us what the differences are between the decision on the forming of the staff of the MUP in the KiM of the 15th of May and the 12th [as interpreted] of June, 1998, which was issued by the chief of the public security department and the decision on the formation of the staff for the suppression of terrorism on the 16th of June, which was adopted by -- which was issued by the minister of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The differences are in the very legal basis on which they were issued. The formation of the staff for the suppression of terrorism and the staff that was organised by the chief of the public security department are different by the nature of their work. The basis for one is Article 10 of the rules on the organisation of the public security department, and the other one has its legal basis in Article 7. And then there are also differences in the composition of the department. The public security department comprises of members from the public security department, and the inter-departmental staff includes both public and state security department officials. The responsibilities are also linked in this way. The staff for the suppression of terrorism is responsible to the minister, and the staff of the public security department is responsible for its work to the chief of the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I made a mistake, so can we make a correction on page 24 of the transcript, line 21. It should say of the 11th of June, 1998, and not the 12th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC
utterances.text: The 12th --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's not for you, this particular thing. Witness, thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Stamp, it's a little early, but would it be more convenient to have the first break now and commence and leave you an uninterrupted session, or would you like to carry on now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was going to ask in the break if the cross-examination could commence tomorrow. I must confess that I have some difficulty with proceeding now, today, for a variety of personal reasons, but I saw on the Defence notification -- on the Defence notification that they had put down four hours. And I had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic is becoming much more responsive to the needs of the Chamber, and we hope you too will follow his example.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But nevertheless, you would like not to continue today, but to continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How long would you anticipate taking?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't think I will go beyond two sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is asked to agree to adjourn today, with a view to the evidence of the witness concluding tomorrow, after Mr. Stamp has cross-examined for no more than two sessions, leaving the remaining session for any re-examination by Mr. Djurdjic and for any inquiries or questions of the Chamber. There are apparently personal reasons which cause Mr. Stamp to make this request. The Chamber bears in mind, of course, the convenience and concerns of both parties and of the witness. Clearly, in the anticipated timetable the witness may have been here until Friday; fortunately, it appears that the -- both parties are agreed that less time is needed to deal with the evidence of the witness than had been anticipated. Mr. Djurdjic, instead of taking the whole of the day today, has finished in less than one session, which is impressive. But of course that's to do with the fact that the witness's evidence is clear, as we have heard it so far, and he has set out the foundation for his reasons and conclusions, both orally and in the written document, which we are to consider in due course admitting into evidence. Those circumstances suggest that it would not be disruptive of the programme of the witness, nor of the due speed with which his evidence is received, if we were to agree to Mr. Stamp's request on the basis that he will have just two sessions tomorrow in which to conclude his cross-examination and that the third session tomorrow will be one in which Mr. Djurdjic could re-examine and the Chamber question, if necessary. That ought to mean that the witness's evidence is concluded tomorrow before the normal time of 1.45 in the day so that the witness will be free to leave actually earlier than could have been anticipated and the whole of the evidence of this witness will have been heard. On that basis, Mr. Stamp, if you're happy with those clearly defined time-limits of two sessions --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm obliged to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- we will agree to the adjournment of today and we will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. I see, Professor, that you've been following what has been discussed, and as we anticipated, this will not inconvenience you but it will mean, I expect, that you can be confident of your evidence finishing tomorrow, which may be to your advantage. And you will have the balance of this morning to your own time. So we will on that basis adjourn now, with a view to the trial continuing at 9.00 tomorrow morning. There will be no more than the first two sessions devoted to the cross-examination by Mr. Stamp tomorrow. On that basis, we adjourn now to resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of May, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.20 a.m.,
